summary: Takashi Hidaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as an open-recruitment researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and held a post as a part-time lecturer at Otani University, attested in 2014.

Takashi Iwata (born 1944) works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University under Akira Hirakawa and at the University of Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler, later serving as assistant professor (circa 1987-1992) and professor (circa 1992-2015) at Waseda.
Takashi Maeda (born 1943) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Taisho University, attested in 1995 and 2006.

Takashi Nakao (1931-2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Rissho University from circa 1950 to 1957 and served as an emeritus professor there from circa 2002 to 2020.

Takashi Ogawa (born 1961) works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (circa 1980-1989) and Peking University (circa 1986-1988), and was an assistant professor at Komazawa University around 1991.

Takashi Yamada (born 1954) specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Hosei University from circa 1973 to 1985 and served as an assistant professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto from circa 1994 to 2004.
Takatoshi Ito (born 1942) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held a professorship at Komazawa University, attested between 1978 and 1981, and again in 1991.
Takatoshi Nakamura specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979 and served as an assistant at Taisho University, attested in 1978.

Takatsugu Hayashi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Delhi (attested 1996) and held posts at Tohoku University (attested 1997), NIT Sendai College (attested 2008), and Hosen Gakuen College as professor (attested 2015).

Takayasu Kimura (1934-2017) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he was attested as a lecturer in 1995, and was also a researcher at the Buzan-ha Institute of Modern Mission in 1995.

Takayasu Suzuki (born 1964) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1984 to 1995 and became a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University around 2006.
Takayoshi Namikawa (born 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University from circa 1966 to 1974 and later served as a professor there from circa 1994 to 2017.

Takayuki Hirosawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, was a group member at Taisho University until 1991, and served as a professor there, attested in 2014.

Takeo Hibino (1914-2007) worked in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (circa 1935-1938) and later held posts at Otemon Gakuin University (circa 1978-1987) and Otemae University (circa 1987-1999).

Takeshi Fujii (born 1955) specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from circa 1974 to 1980 and later held a post there from circa 1995 to 2020.

Takeshi Umehara (1925-2019) worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University and Nagoya University, subsequently holding posts at Ryukoku University, Ritsumeikan University as professor, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies as director general, and the Institute of Technologists.

Takudo Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as a researcher at the Jodo Shu Research Institute, attested in 2005, and as a specially appointed full-time lecturer at Taisho University, attested in 2015.

Takushu Sugimoto (born 1935) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD from Tohoku University, and held posts at Komazawa University, Kinjo University, and Kanazawa University, where he became emeritus professor circa 2000.

Tan Chung (1929-2024) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Indology. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Delhi (circa 1964-1978) and head of Chinese and Japanese Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (circa 1978-1994).

Tansen Sen specializes in history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Peking University and the University of Pennsylvania, where he completed his PhD under Victor H. Mair, and held a post at Baruch College, attested in 2003.
